hypothesis: Current Trigger-6 claim path semantics prevent duplicate files but do not prevent semantic duplicate objectives when workers choose different research_id values.
counterhypothesis: The second WP803/E1 claim was created only because the first claim was not yet visible at the second worker's base/parent, so the existing path law is sufficient and the event is only a concurrency visibility race.

first_claim.objective: WP803 external source audit for leak-resistant held-out sequential prediction, abstention/UNKNOWN and public-information baselines

second_claim.objective: WP803 external primary research/benchmark mechanisms to strengthen held-out world-model prediction evaluation

observations.ancestry_check: Fetching the first claim at ref 31b2f0c8c1fe13e2e3962c6cdabb9e2f61b57c53 succeeds and returns the full first claim. Therefore the first claim was visible in the exact parent of the second claim commit.

falsification: Counterhypothesis rejected at repository evidence scope: visibility lag is not required to explain the duplicate. The second claim used a different research_id path despite the first materially overlapping E1 claim already being present in its parent.
architecture_implication: A canonical semantic objective key must be distinct from research provenance ID. Create-only coordination should lock the normalized objective key, while research_id remains lineage metadata.
required_next_test: Implement a pure deterministic objective_key_v1 normalizer fixture and verify different research_id values with the same typed objective inputs collide to one create-only path while genuinely different stage/source/discriminator objectives remain distinct.
